title: Sandiacre Lancaster Memorial
memorial_details: Stained-glass window to Sgt I.K. Doncaster, KIA 22 October 1943 (date on CSV states 12/10/43 — verify against Chorley; Kassel raid was 22/10/43), in St Giles Church, Sandiacre, Derbyshire.
narrative: Lancaster EE196 of 166 Squadron, coded AS-Z, departed Kirmington on the Kassel raid of 22 October 1943. The aircraft was possibly shot down at 5000m NW of Holzminden by Hauptmann Eduard Schröder of 12/NJG3 at 2103, his third claim. The aircraft crashed at Brakelsiek, 2km west of Schwalenberg. Six crew were killed; one survived as a prisoner of war. Sgt I.K. Doncaster of Sandiacre, on the Nottinghamshire/Derbyshire border, is commemorated in St Giles Church.
cause_of_loss: Possibly shot down by night fighter — Hptm Eduard Schröder (12/NJG3), 3rd claim; crashed at Brakelsiek
notes: Date conflict in source post (12/10/43 vs Kassel raid 22/10/43) — verify against Chorley BCL Vol. 4 before publishing. Sandiacre is on the Notts/Derbys border.
